_comment: Only-Short Grid Bot config (v1.1). Secrets and environment-selection live in .env (see .env.example), loaded via python-dotenv -- NOT in this file: BYBIT_API_KEY, BYBIT_API_SECRET, USE_TESTNET, SYMBOL, GRID_STEP_PERCENT. The grid is 100% dynamic: no fixed price list. grid_step_pct defines the geometric spacing between levels (Level_N = base_price * (1 + grid_step_pct/100)^N); base_price (Range 0) is re-anchored to the live market price at startup and after every Take Profit reset, so it is never a config value either.
_comment_symbol_timeframe: symbol and grid_step_pct below are fallback defaults, overridden by .env's SYMBOL / GRID_STEP_PERCENT when set. timeframe drives the grid-evaluation clock automatically: '5m' evaluates at XX:05:01/XX:10:01/... (fast testing), '1h' evaluates at HH:00:01 (production).
_comment_grid_step_table_pct: Overrides grid_step_pct ONLY going UP from Range 0 (Range +1, +2, +3, ...) with a per-step percentage instead of one fixed value: entry i is the distance from Range i to Range i+1 (entry 0 = Range 0->+1, entry 1 = Range +1->+2, etc). Once Range climbs past the table's length, every further step repeats the LAST entry forever. Going DOWN from Range 0 (Range -1, -2, ...) always uses the fixed grid_step_pct above, unaffected by this table. Add/remove/edit entries freely -- any length works. Leave as [] to disable and make the grid fully symmetric again (grid_step_pct on both sides, the pre-v1.3.1 behavior) -- currently disabled, every range (up and down) uses the flat 0.2% grid_step_pct above.
_comment_trailing_stop: enabled=false -> FIXED take profit: closes the whole position at market the instant mark_price first drops activation_pct% BELOW the current Break-Even NETTO price (already fee/funding-adjusted) -- single threshold, no arming, no trailing (distance_pct is ignored in this mode). enabled=true -> SHORT-only TRAILING stop: arms at that same activation_pct% threshold, then pins the initial stop distance_pct% ABOVE the arming price and only ever trails down on new lows. Both percentages are real PRICE percentages, not leveraged-margin percentages.
_comment_auto_compound: Legacy sizing: multiplies base_notional_usdt by (1+percentage/100) on every completed cycle, regardless of account performance. Ignored entirely while equity_based_sizing.enabled=true below (kept here only so you can revert by flipping that flag off).
_comment_equity_based_sizing: Replaces auto_compound above when enabled=true: at the start of every cycle (bootstrap and every immediate re-open after a close), re-reads the account's real total equity (Bybit V5 totalEquity, all collateral assets combined) and sets base_notional_usdt to percentage% of it. Self-correcting -- grows only if the account actually grew, shrinks on its own after a drawdown -- instead of compounding blindly by cycle count. base_notional_usdt above is only the seed value used before the first equity read, or if a read ever fails.
_comment_eth_spot_accumulator: Fully optional, isolated hedge (see eth_spot_accumulator.py) -- at every new cycle's genesis, spends 100% of the free USDT balance on a single SPOT market buy of ETH (never touches the short/perpetual strategy). No minimum threshold: it always attempts the purchase with whatever free USDT is available (if > 0), and simply lets Bybit accept or reject the order -- a rejection (e.g. below the exchange's real minimum) is absorbed by the same fail-safe as any other failure, with zero impact on the main strategy. Set enabled=false to disable without removing the code; delete eth_spot_accumulator.py entirely to remove the feature.
_comment_notifier: Fully optional, isolated Telegram notification (see notifier.py) -- fires once per closed cycle (take profit or trailing stop) with cycle_id, net PnL, total equity (USDT+EUR), and the collateral breakdown per coin. Requires TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID in .env (never here); if missing, silently does nothing. Set enabled=false to disable without removing the code; delete notifier.py entirely to remove the feature.
_comment_grid_reindex: enabled=true (default): Range 0 follows the Break-Even, re-pointed after every fill -- Fibonacci offsets are always measured relative to wherever Break-Even currently sits, so the multiplier effectively 'resets' each time Break-Even catches up to a new band. enabled=false: the grid stays TRULY static for the whole cycle -- zero_index never moves from 0, so every offset (and Fibonacci level) is always measured from the cycle's ORIGINAL anchor price. Price quotes/levels themselves are identical either way; this only changes which level is LABELED Range 0, and therefore how fast Fibonacci sizing grows over a long, heavily-mediated cycle.
_comment_stress_test: High-frequency time-acceleration stress test mode. When enabled=true it REPLACES the normal timeframe/candle-close scheduler: all ranges evaluate at base_interval_sec (flat, no per-range table) UNLESS RSI tick mode is active, in which case grid orders fire every tick_mode_interval_sec instead. base_interval_sec=2 combined with the 'one order per range per cycle' rule turns this into effectively REACTIVE evaluation: as soon as price enters a range that hasn't fired yet this cycle, the corresponding Fibonacci order fires within ~2s, instead of waiting for a slow timer -- revisiting an already-used range is a cheap no-op (logged at DEBUG level, not INFO, to avoid flooding the log at this cadence). rsi_enabled=false disables the RSI reading/tick-mode entirely (base cadence only, forever) while leaving everything else in stress-test mode (base cadence, Neutral Zone, unlimited_fib_level) untouched -- flip it back to true to re-arm RSI/tick-mode later without touching anything else. When rsi_enabled=true, tick mode is triggered by an RSI(rsi_period) reading on rsi_timeframe crossing UP through rsi_overbought_threshold (a fresh crossing from below -- staying overbought does not re-trigger it), and stays on until the position's Break-Even price catches up to the market's current grid band, at which point the base cadence resumes. unlimited_fib_level=true removes the risk.max_fib_level safety cap for this mode only. Set enabled=false to fall back to the normal production scheduler/cap untouched.
